conclusion.question: is django-15572's fifteen-of-fifteen failure a first-answer compliance failure, or does the registered contract force an answer longer than the bound?
conclusion.failure_class: first-answer length-compliance failure: the model wrote an explanatory answer far past the bound, and the single billed retry shortened it substantially but never enough, so the answer closed empty
why_not_a_contract_defect: the shortest line that satisfies the frozen regex, all three required literals and the single-line prefix is 75 characters, leaving 85 characters of room under the bound; a compliant answer demonstrably exists and was demonstrated before the batch ran

django-15572's shortest compliant line is the longest of the three by only 2 characters over the longest of the other two, and the other two tasks share the same bound; django-16255 in particular accepted 5 of 12 first attempts at the same bound

the failure is not a length budget the task cannot meet: the model's own first proposals rendered to 248-285 characters on the line the bound is applied to, that is 88-125 characters past the bound, and the text they carried is explanatory prose rather than required literals: the first proposal declared the required fact list in full and left no required literal out of the candidate line on any of the fifteen samples
why_it_is_a_compliance_failure: every one of the fifteen reached samples of django-15572 was rejected on the first attempt with the single class over_160_chars: {'over_160_chars': 15}

the one billed retry was spent on every one of those fifteen samples and still produced a rendered line of 166-194 characters, every one of them past the bound, so the answers closed empty for the whole task

the retry did most of the shortening and still fell short: the rendered line fell from 248-285 characters to 166-194, a reduction of roughly a third that still left every sample 6 to 34 characters over the bound, which is the signature of a shortest-plausible rewrite rather than of a rewrite aimed at a target below the bound

the same configuration, the same arms, the same first prompt and the same retry diagnostic accepted 24 of the 24 reached samples of the other two tasks, with first-attempt acceptance {'sitemap_callable_lastmod': {'samples_reached': 12, 'first_attempt_accepted': 5, 'first_attempt_acceptance_rate': 0.4167, 'render_reasons': {'accepted_first': 5, 'accepted_retry': 7}}, 'query_utils_unregister_lookup': {'samples_reached': 12, 'first_attempt_accepted': 0, 'first_attempt_acceptance_rate': 0.0, 'render_reasons': {'accepted_retry': 12}}}, so neither the prompt nor the diagnostic is generally unusable

the bound reaches the model once in the first prompt, inside the contract prompt's closing sentence, and the fixed sentence that carries 'at most 160 characters' is replaced by the frozen v17 prompt adaptation before the prompt is sent, so nothing in the prompt states that exceeding the bound is a hard rejection rather than a preference, and nothing gives a working target below it
